title: Best three days
scenario: Find the best 3-day stretch — the three days in a row with the biggest total.

intro.job: Find the best 3-day stretch — the three days in a row with the biggest total.

idea.rule: A window that slides has to lose the day that leaves — add the new day, subtract the old one, or the total is a lie.
idea.detail: Add up the first 3 days once. Then slide the window one day at a time: a new day comes in on the right, and the oldest day falls off on the left. Instead of re-adding all three, add the newcomer and subtract the leaver — the total always covers exactly 3 days.

watch.code:
k = 3
total = sum(nums[:k])
best = total
for i in range(k, len(nums)):
    total += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
    best = max(best, total)
print(best)

model_restatement: Find the largest sum of any 3 consecutive days.

clarify.question: What if there are fewer than 3 days?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Add up the first 3 days. Then for each later day, add it to the total and keep the best total. Print it.

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 1 (i = 3): after line 5, what is total?
With the fix — iteration 1: after line 5, what is total?

why_line: total only ever grows: day 3 is added but day 0 never leaves, so after one slide total covers 4 days (2 + 1 + 5 + 1 = 9), not the 3-day window [1, 5, 1] = 7.

explain.rule: A window that only adds is a train that picks up passengers at every stop and never lets anyone off — the headcount stops meaning 'three days'.
explain.bridge: When the window slides one day to the right, which day has to leave?

fix.rule: total += nums[i] - nums[i - k]: the new day in, the day k back out — always exactly k days.

walk.gloss: Slide: i is the day coming in.
Add the new day, subtract the one that just left the window.
Keep the best 3-day total so far.

fix.recommended:
k = 3
total = sum(nums[:k])
best = total
for i in range(k, len(nums)):
    total += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
    best = max(best, total)
print(best)

alternatives.code:
k = 3
best = sum(nums[:k])
for i in range(1, len(nums) - k + 1):
    best = max(best, sum(nums[i:i + k]))
print(best)
alternatives.note: Re-add every window from scratch — correct, but it repeats work (slow for big k).
